judging.rubric: Integer scores 0–10. Tend toward 5 for delivering the brief; reserve 9–10 for polished work. Specific justification at most 400 characters.
judging.noArtifact: Record noArtifact with null scores. Do not award seeded input files as generated output.
judging.reviewPolicy: Review failed artifacts as well as passes. Read blinded packets where practical; record limitations and clipping. Runtime checks and source evidence support the review. Keep four rubric aggregates separate from fixed capability scores and performance.
judging.blinding: Unblinded regression triage; advisory current-session judgments.

notes: Four separate advisory rubric means; no overall quality mean. Missing artifacts have null scores and are outside artifact means, inside raw denominators.
Decode uses only facts.perf.derived.genTokensPerSec. No meanTokensPerSec fallback, zero fill, maximum selection or token-stream coalescing.
Bolt uses exact request-derived llama.cpp decode/prefill. MLX decode is an active-stream estimate; prefill is unavailable.
Generated-token volume is engine-log-derived for Bolt and incompletely sampled for MLX. Billing-tracker tokens are a separate incompletely covered stream.
First-artifact latency is the raw attributed-write proxy, not completed-output latency. Binary image availability is audited separately.
Wall times retain failed attempts, tools and recovery. Admission probes are excluded. Process RSS is not GPU memory; GPU telemetry unavailable.

reportMarkdown:
# Five-model Gezel scorecard — completed October 26, 2026

**All 165 trials are complete and reviewed: 110 raw passes, 55 failures, 158 scored artifacts and seven missing outputs recorded with null judgments.** Nemotron 3.5 Bolt and Gemma E4B tie for the most task passes, at 26/33. E4B has the slightly better fixed composite, lower median task time and lower median peak process memory. Bolt is a strong general-purpose candidate on this device, but its three missing outputs and image/recovery failures prevent calling the integration fully reliable.

The largest practical concern is the gap between passing a gate and delivering a usable artifact. Some passing websites were placeholders; some passing games had broken combat, incorrect result messages or invisible moves. There are also false-negative gates and repair-policy defects. These results support fixing those shared paths before further sampling tuning. This campaign establishes their presence in the current build; it does **not** establish which were introduced by the recent updates.

## Comparison

These are the installed integrations on an Apple M5 Max with 128 GiB unified memory. Bolt uses llama.cpp Metal; the other four use MLX. Engines, model formats and provider behavior are therefore part of the comparison.

| Model | Raw passes | Fixed composite /10 | Median task time, all trials | Median decode tokens/s | Median peak process RSS |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B Q4 | 26/33 (78.8%) | 8.23 | 153.6 s | 72.0 | 10.0 GiB |
| Gemma 4 E4B Q4 | 26/33 (78.8%) | 8.41 | 138.3 s | ~79.0 | 8.1 GiB |
| Gemma 4 E2B Q4 | 14/33 (42.4%) | 6.78 | 99.1 s | ~115.5 | 7.1 GiB |
| Gemma 4 12B Q4 | 23/33 (69.7%) | 8.04 | 254.3 s | ~38.0 | 10.7 GiB |
| Qwen 3.5 9B Q4 | 21/33 (63.6%) | 7.58 | 158.5 s | ~63.5 | 8.0 GiB |

Bolt decode uses request-derived llama.cpp timings. The tilde denotes MLX active-stream estimates. RSS is process memory, not GPU memory. Decode sample counts are 33, 33, 32, 33 and 30 respectively; unavailable values are excluded, never replaced with total-token throughput. The fixed composite is the harness's capability/behavior score, distinct from the artifact judgments below.

My interpretation of this run:

- **E4B and Bolt are the strongest general-purpose candidates.** E4B completed all three data tasks and had one missing output. Bolt completed all schema, symptom-debug, incident, runbook and planning trials, and was the only model to pass one failing-tests-spec trial. Their small aggregate differences are descriptive, not a statistically established ranking.
- **E2B trades substantial task coverage for speed.** Its fastest decode and shortest task median coexist with only 14 passes. Fast failures make aggregate speed look better; this is not evidence that it completes the same work faster.
- **12B improves some artifact quality without dominating task coverage.** Its HTML mean is highest, although still well below a polished result. Its long failed attempts drive the all-trial median to 254 seconds; successful trials have a 117-second median. Its data mean covers only two outputs.
- **Qwen is uneven across task types.** Its pet-shop artifacts were comparatively stronger, but schema migration, data wrangling and conflict synthesis each finished 0/3. It also produced long repair loops, including a 2,672-second failed data task.

## Scenario coverage

Every entry is raw passes out of three repetitions. No verdict was replaced by a diagnostic counterfactual.

| Scenario | Bolt | E4B | E2B | 12B | Qwen |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Tic-tac-toe | 2 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| Pet-shop website and image | 2 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 3 |
| Tank combat | 2 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 3 |
| Schema migration | 3 | 3 | 0 | 3 | 0 |
| Failing tests from specification | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Symptom debugging | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| Data wrangling | 2 | 3 | 0 | 2 | 0 |
| Incident postmortem | 3 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
| Runbook anomaly | 3 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 3 |
| Plan and estimate | 3 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 3 |
| Conflicting-source synthesis | 2 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 0 |

All 55 failed trials were reviewed. The harness classified all 55 as model failures, with no infrastructure/operator/grader exclusions inside this cohort. That label does not establish pure model causation: the investigations below demonstrate framework and evaluator contributions. Genuine model defects also remain, including compilation failures, incorrect CSV/date handling, unsupported incident facts and violations of explicit source-quarantine rules.

## Artifact judging

Judging used the active Codex session and the frozen [judge protocol](judge-protocol.json), with source inspection, browser interaction and deterministic checks where relevant. Each rubric has four integer axes from 0 to 10; about 5 means delivering the brief, and 9–10 is reserved for polished work. Means below average those axes and then trials **within the same rubric**. There is no overall quality average across rubrics.

| Model | HTML quality /10 | Code quality /10 | Data quality /10 | Document quality /10 | Missing outputs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Bolt | 2.58 (6) | 4.78 (9) | 4.00 (3) | 4.17 (12) | 3 |
| E4B | 2.56 (9) | 4.84 (8) | 4.50 (3) | 4.02 (12) | 1 |
| E2B | 2.25 (8) | 4.14 (9) | 2.50 (3) | 3.73 (12) | 1 |
| 12B | 3.19 (9) | 4.50 (9) | 4.75 (2) | 4.08 (12) | 1 |
| Qwen | 2.78 (9) | 3.67 (9) | 2.62 (2) | 4.06 (12) | 1 |

Parentheses are scored-output counts. Missing outputs remain in the raw pass denominator but are excluded from artifact means. These are therefore quality estimates conditional on producing an output, especially relevant to Bolt's HTML and 12B/Qwen's data results. Failed artifacts were scored, too. Unchanged seeded implementations and helper-only attempts did not receive credit as completed deliverables.

The seven missing-output records are Bolt repetition 2 tic-tac-toe and tank combat, Bolt repetition 3 pet shop, E2B repetition 2 pet shop, 12B repetition 2 data, E4B repetition 3 failing-tests-spec, and Qwen repetition 3 data. The last two retain qualitative evidence about altered tests/helper attempts, with null deliverable scores.

The review was advisory and unblinded for regression triage. The artifact input cap was 20 KiB per trial; clipping and omitted files are recorded individually. In particular, the first E4B data review clipped the middle of its final script. Review scores are not an independent blinded model leaderboard or a claim of exhaustive verification. [All judgments](codex-inline-judge.json) preserve the axes, rationales, evidence and artifact hashes.

## Performance and measurement limits

| Model | All-trial wall median [min–max], seconds | Passing-trial wall median, seconds | First tool median, seconds | First token median, seconds | Median tool calls |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Bolt | 153.6 [27.5–1553.6] | 124.5 (26) | 14.8 | 8.6 | 10 |
| E4B | 138.3 [32.5–1165.8] | 118.8 (26) | 16.3 | 10.5 | 13 |
| E2B | 99.1 [27.6–1194.7] | 47.6 (14) | 12.9 | 8.6 | 15 |
| 12B | 254.3 [43.1–1153.6] | 117.3 (23) | 29.9 | 16.9 | 10 |
| Qwen | 158.5 [43.0–2672.2] | 133.3 (21) | 23.6 | 20.5 | 14 |

All columns have 33 samples per model except passing-trial times, whose counts are shown. Wall time retains tools, failed attempts and recovery, while admission probes are excluded. The 165 task wall times total approximately 12.0 hours. Per-scenario repetitions, all metric ranges/sample counts and token coverage are in [the detailed tables](scorecard-tables.md); exact values and provenance are in [scorecard-data.json](scorecard-data.json).

Bolt's median measured prefill was **2,514 tokens/s**, ranging from 1,977 to 3,493 across 33 trials. MLX prefill is unavailable. MLX generation sampling and the billing tracker have incomplete, different coverage; neither was substituted for or combined with the other. Engine logged/sampled generation totals were 294,715 / 251,658 / 274,997 / 240,116 / 220,564 in the table's model order. Tracker token totals are separately reported with coverage of 26 / 27 / 29 / 31 / 31 trials. A sampled observation in all 33 trials does not mean all requests or tokens were measured. These are not complete cost totals.

The raw first-attributed-artifact medians are 44.2 / 52.3 / 34.0 / 61.5 / 64.0 seconds, with counts 30 / 33 / 32 / 33 / 33. This is a file-write proxy, **not finished-output latency**: it can include helper or seeded-file writes and misses binary writes lacking actor attribution. The final [timing audit](artifact-timing-audit.json) found eight trials with successful image events, four of which saved an image before the raw metric. Qwen repetition 3 pet shop, for example, saved its first image at 137.785 seconds while the raw first-artifact field says 319.943 seconds. An earlier image does not imply an earlier completed website.

Only `genTokensPerSec` was used for decode. The generic throughput fallback can include input tokens, producing misleading values such as hundreds of tokens/s; it was not used for the three Qwen schema trials or E2B repetition 3 runbook with unavailable decode. Mac GPU utilization/memory telemetry was unavailable. Process RSS and local zero-dollar billing cannot establish GPU memory requirements, energy consumption or operating cost.

## Framework and evaluator findings

The campaign documented **32 findings**, with captured traces, isolated probes, controls and causal limits in [REGRESSION-NOTES.md](REGRESSION-NOTES.md). They are not 32 proven recent regressions, and not every finding caused a raw failure. The initial five trials were inspected before the rest of the frozen campaign continued. No new engine-startup, OOM or GPU-crash pattern emerged; normal idle engine exits were distinguished from failures.

The highest-value follow-up work is:

1. **Preserve the tools needed to finish and repair work.** Image handoff can lose `generate_image` through tiny tool caps or a generic “save file first” classification. A captured data-repair path loses execution tools and can end after writing a helper. Synthesis repair says to read the output first while another layer requires five source reads first. Incident repair can expose retrieval without editing. These are shared policy contradictions, not evidence that every affected model lacks the underlying capability. Findings 3, 15, 20 and 24.
2. **Correct native tool parsing and failure validation.** The legacy JSON parser corrupts escapes in four of five complete native Gemma tool-call controls, whereas the native parser preserves all five. The raw pre-parser body was unavailable for the corresponding live symptom, so live causality is limited. Separately, parse-only validation accepts duplicate declarations that Node rejects. Findings 14 and 23.
